Steam is produced at 950 °F and 1,550 psia. The configuration includes a high-pressure and medium-pressure turbine that drives high powered equipment such as the ammonia production compressors, refrigeration compressors, and air compressor. Additional electricity for the remaining auxiliary loads of the plant was purchased from the grid at $65.2/MWh, according to the “Fuel Prices for Selected Feedstocks in NETL Studies” (NETL, 2025c). The delivered price of electricity reflects the price paid by an entity to procure utility electricity services and comprises generation, transmission, and distribution components. The price is based on regional-level forecasts for the Midcontinent Independent System Operator region for 2030 delivered industrial electricity reference case, reported in 2023$/MWh (NETL, 2025c). 25 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 2.9 LIFE CYCLE ANALYSIS APPROACH This section describes the design parameters and data sources for the LCA portion of study. The LCA presented herein complies with ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 guidelines (ISO, 2006a; ISO, 2006b). 2.9.1 Goal and Scope The goal of this LCA is to evaluate the life cycle impacts of natural gas-based ammonia production. The evaluation focuses on three production pathways: SMR, SMR with CCS, and ATR with CCS. Geographical scenarios, specifically U.S. average and Midwest-specific, are analyzed for each production pathway to determine geographical impacts of upstream natural gas and electricity. 2.9.2 Function and Functional Unit The functional unit for this study is defined as 1 kg of ammonia. Specifically, the product is commercial grade (C-grade) ammonia produced at a temperature of -33°C and a pressure of 0.14 MPa. This functional unit reflects standard production and storage conditions for ammonia, making it a suitable basis for comparison and analysis across different production pathways and scenarios. 2.9.3 System Boundary The LCA study adopts a cradle-to-gate system boundary that begins with the extraction of raw materials and ends at the production of ammonia at the plant gate. The full system boundary is displayed in Exhibit 2-11. Exhibit 2-11. System boundary diagram for ammonia production The LCA system boundary includes upstream material production and transportation, production and transportation of feedstocks such as natural gas and electricity, water treatment, and the production of process consumables, as well as on-site processes including 26 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION feed processing and reactor systems, syngas cleanup, ammonia synthesis, and pipeline transport and saline aquifer sequestration of captured CO .
